constraints.text: rowPresent => recState /= rsNone (unless the record was dropped): no row outlives its record (no BadOrphan)
constraints.verifiedBy: the first two make delete_session / append_wtmp fail once and assert the record (status().sessions) stays while the row is still readable, then the next end removes row and record; the third asserts a second connection cannot recreate the row after the end

constraints.text: ttyOwner = tOld => recState /= rsNone (unless the record was dropped): the name does not outlive the record
constraints.verifiedBy: both assert owner() is None after the end / the expiry

constraints.text: newLive => ttyOwner = tNew: an end never frees a name another session took (owner-checked release)
constraints.verifiedBy: the test releases the old session's reservation, reserves the name for kai:someone-else, ends the session, and asserts the owner is still kai:someone-else

constraints.text: outboxN + flightN + sessN + userN + shownN + lostN + strandedN = issuedN: an end files the held batch and drains the session inbox into the user's mailbox; a graceful stop files the outbox back; a process loss loses the outbox and the read in flight; a drop of the record strands the session inbox (strandedN counts it; it is not recovered)
constraints.verifiedBy: the first holds an unconfirmed batch (consuming relay) and asserts it is in the user mailbox after the end; the second asserts both inbox messages reach the user mailbox; the two tests of the graceful stop (test_shutdown_reads.py, test_claude_expiry.py) assert the stop side of the equation: the held batch and the settled read's mail are back in the relay. The last asserts the crash side: the held batch is lost and the mail still in the relay reaches the user's mailbox at retention. The late broadcast fetch has no test: see limitsWithoutTest. shownN is not asserted. flightN is asserted only through the first graceful-stop test (a read mid-fetch when the stop arrives)

constraints.text: recState = rsEnding => endRun = currentRun: a replaced run cannot end the session
constraints.verifiedBy: the end test: a connection of run a1 after a2 replaced it gets session_replaced (or is closed), row and owner are unchanged and one session remains; then the current run ends it. The ledger test shows the refusal is permanent

constraints.text: EndOwnSession: a connection of the current run begins the end
constraints.verifiedBy: end by the current-run connection removes row and name; a shell's session is refused invalid_params, which the model does not have (a stricter code)

constraints.text: EndRefused: a connection of a replaced run changes nothing
constraints.verifiedBy: after the refused end the test asserts row present, owner unchanged, one session in status

constraints.text: ExpireClaude: a dormant record with no connection, aged to retention, begins the end
constraints.verifiedBy: the first closes the client (no connection, dormant), a sweep at retention 3600 leaves it, a sweep at 0 removes row, name and record and appends one logout; the second shows a connected session is never expired; the third shows a reattached session is not expired (it shows the reattach wins, not that the age restarts from zero)

constraints.text: DeleteRow, ReleaseTty, AppendLogout, FileOutbox, FinishEnd: each effect of an end, and the record stays until all are done
constraints.verifiedBy: one test per effect; the failure tests make delete_session and append_wtmp fail once; the concurrency test parks the first end mid-effect and asserts one logout. A failure of the refile or the drain is not injected

constraints.text: NewHello: the new session of a clear takes the name only after the old end is complete (the goal needs an EndOwnSession step: ownEnded)
constraints.verifiedBy: the first test sends the old end, then the new hello, and asserts the name was free after the end and is then held by the new session; the second sends the new hello first and asserts its claim of the old name is refused while the old session holds it. The model's hello is the daemon-side name claim; the client's wait for the end's reply is not tested here

constraints.text: retention and end: enabled(ExpireClaude) at retention; every owed end step and the finish enabled; a failed end is finished by the next
constraints.verifiedBy: expiry at retention happens; a refused expiry leaves the record and the next sweep removes it; a failed end is finished by the next end

constraints.text: shownDormant = zfalse: held mail is not consumed when nobody is connected
constraints.verifiedBy: a reply is handed over (request_held), never confirmed, the client closes, a new connection reads and finds the message still unread. It shows no consumption without a confirming client, which is what the model's connected-client guard stands for

constraints.text: ProcessLoss (live or dormant, no read running): a crash loses the daemon's outbox; the relay's mail and the record are not lost (PL-1753)
constraints.verifiedBy: read on main 8cc73dd. _kill closes the listener and the relays, cancels the sweep and the retry, and patches SessionTable.release so no connection is noted as left: no hand-back, no cleanup, as a kill. The first holds an unconfirmed batch (request_held returns, so the read has already replied: the batch is in the outbox, not in flight), writes a second message, kills and restarts; at retention 0 the mailbox holds only the second message. The second kills a session with a connection on it and asserts the restored session reaches retention, its row goes, its mail reaches the mailbox and its record goes. It is an in-process kill, not a process death: medium. A crash during a read (flightN > 0: the fetch consumed the mail and the read has not replied) is not exercised; see the row below

constraints.text: ProcessLoss during a read (flightN > 0): a crash after the consuming fetch and before the read replies loses the mail in flight (and the outbox)
constraints.verifiedBy: no test. test_a_crash_loses_the_outbox_but_not_the_mail_still_in_the_relay waits for request_held to return before it kills, so it crashes after the read replied; no test kills while a fetch is stalled. Counted as uncovered

constraints.text: GracefulStop (settled? = ztrue): the held outbox of every session, and mail of a read that settled, is filed back to the relay before the daemon closes; the relay's mail is untouched
constraints.verifiedBy: read on main 5684388. The first: a consuming relay whose fetch_user_inbox consumes the mail and stalls 0.3 s; harness.daemon.stop() is called while a read is mid-fetch (consumed set); a new BiffDaemon queried by a cli client returns the mail: the settle step waits for the read and the hand-over files it. The second is parametrised over consuming and non-consuming relays: a seat holds an unconfirmed batch (request_held 'read'), the daemon is stopped and revived, and a reattached read returns it. The third holds three unconfirmed messages, makes the first publish at stop fail, and asserts m2 and m3 are given back (one refused message does not drop the rest; the refused one stays held and is logged). The second also asserts the session is restored from its record, dormant, before any hello (RestoreRecord); the first and third restart a daemon and read the mail back through a client

constraints.text: GracefulStop (settled? = zfalse, lastStop = sTimedOut): the settle wait is bounded and the stop returns; held mail is filed back; mail the read had not yet taken stays in the relay; session mail already in the outbox survives
constraints.verifiedBy: the first sets SETTLE_SECONDS to 0.1, holds m1 (request_held), writes m2, and starts a read that hangs before taking m2; stop() completes inside 0.4 s and a restarted daemon reads m1 and m2 (m1 filed back, m2 never taken). The second makes the broadcast fetch stick after the session fetch took the session mail; stop() runs out the wait and a restarted daemon reads the session mail (SessionFetch put it into the outbox before the broadcast fetch). Neither test makes a fetch consume mail and then outlive the wait: that loss (lostN with sTimedOut) is the window PL-1777 tracks, see limitsWithoutTest

constraints.text: RestoreRecord: a kept record whose repository is there and whose relay row is listed is built again at start, dormant; retention resumes from the stored dormant time; a session that had a connection starts a fresh retention; the claimed run comes back
constraints.verifiedBy: the first closes the client, restarts, and at retention 0 the unread session mail is in the mailbox and the row gone; the second restarts, sees the session held with no connection, reattaches and ends it, mail drained and record deleted; the third marks dormant_since ten days ago, restarts, and a sweep at three days ends it; the fourth restarts a session that had a connection and a sweep at three days leaves its row (fresh retention); the fifth opens two runs and the restored run is a2; the last stores and clears dormant_since. The model's retention age is paused while the daemon is down (the code's runs on): see limitsWithoutTest

constraints.text: RestoreFail: a start that cannot build the session keeps the record and counts the failure; retried at 5/15/45 s while running and at the next start
constraints.verifiedBy: the first fails one resolve with a relay error and the session is present after the retry; the second breaks the configuration of an existing repository: the session is absent and its record kept, and after the fix a restart restores it; the third makes the registration fail: the record keeps its old dormant time with failed_starts 1; the fourth restores the good session beside a hanging and a failing one; the last counts 1, 2. The retry delays are shortened by the tests, not asserted as 5/15/45

constraints.text: DropRecord: dRepoGone (repository directory gone: dropped at once), dRowGone (the relay lists no row: the session ended, or aged out while down), dFailedStarts (MAX_FAILED_STARTS starts in a row failed)
constraints.verifiedBy: the first restarts with a resolver that fails for /work/missing-soon, a directory that does not exist: the record is gone after one start (the unusable-configuration test, whose directory exists, keeps its record: that is RestoreFail); the second deletes the relay row and restarts: the session is not held and no record remains; the third sets MAX_FAILED_STARTS 2 and fails every start: the record stays after the first and is gone after the second; the fourth sets 3 and makes the registration fail: the record is dropped on the third start. The model bounds the count at 2; the code's 5 is a constant the tests change

constraints.text: HelloFirst: after a start whose restore failed, a hello for the session arrives during the retry and wins; the restore leaves it alone and the failure count is cleared (BiffDaemon.start restores before it serves, so no hello comes first at the first attempt)
constraints.verifiedBy: a restart with one failed resolve, then a connect and a close before the retry: after the retry the record's dormant_since is the new disconnect, not the old record

constraints.text: a record is kept from its hello to its end; a hello whose record cannot be written is refused and leaves no session
constraints.verifiedBy: the first sees the record after the hello and none after the end; the second blocks the directory: the hello is refused with a message naming the record and a retry keeps it; the third refuses a hello and writes to the user: no row lists the refused session; the fourth makes the delete fail: the end still ends and logs it (the stale record is dropped at the next start, DropRecord with dRowGone)

limitsWithoutTest.text: DropRecord: the mail waiting in the relay inbox of a dropped session stays there (strandedN)
limitsWithoutTest.reason: a deliberate limit of the code: the relay is not stored in the record, so a drop cannot forward the mail. The model counts it as stranded, not as conserved, and only a drop strands. No test asserts the mail stays after a drop; it is stated, not repaired

limitsWithoutTest.text: RowAgesOut, TtyAgesOut: the relay row and the name age out by the relay's own lifetime, independently of the record: while the daemon is down (the record outlives the name) or after a drop; the retention age is paused while down
limitsWithoutTest.reason: relay behaviour, outside biffd; the model's age does not run while the daemon is down (the code resumes from the stored dormant time, which keeps running), a conservative simplification. The local relay's name reservation has no lifetime, so there TtyAgesOut does not happen. PL-1777 is the open residual (deadline remainder, spill)

limitsWithoutTest.text: GracefulStop with settled? = zfalse and mail in flight (lostN > 0, lastStop = sTimedOut): a read whose broadcast fetch consumed the user's mail and outlives the settle wait loses it
limitsWithoutTest.reason: the window the code cannot close without a further change (PL-1777: the late broadcast fetch). The session mail is not in it: SessionFetch holds it in the outbox first, which test_session_mail_a_read_took_before_a_stuck_broadcast_fetch_survives_a_stop asserts. No test asserts the loss itself, because it would pin a defect. The model's loss is of the broadcast fetch only (BroadcastFetch, flightN); the session fetch (MailFetch) enters the outbox atomically

limitsWithoutTest.text: Handback refile budget (REFILE_SECONDS, 15 s) spent: the held messages not yet filed are dropped and logged
limitsWithoutTest.reason: the deadline remainder is lost with the process (PL-1777). test_slow_publishes_at_stop_end_at_a_total_budget_and_are_logged asserts the stop ends at the budget and logs the count, not that the remainder survives. The model has no transition for it yet: a spill transition (the remainder written to local storage) will be modelled with the fix

limitsWithoutTest.text: claude-session-end-unordered-owned.tex: the owner check alone keeps the new session's name
limitsWithoutTest.reason: model result (2,351 states, invariant holds); the code's check is covered by test_a_name_another_session_took_is_not_freed_by_the_end

limitsWithoutTest.text: claude-session-end-nograceful.tex: a graceful stop that skips the hand-back violates conservation
limitsWithoutTest.reason: model result (50 states to the violation; counterexample MailArrive, MailFetch, GracefulStopForget); the code's hand-back is covered by the graceful-stop tests above

limitsWithoutTest.text: claude-session-end-noflight.tex and -noflight-counted.tex: a settled stop that drops the read's mail (uncounted: conservation is violated; counted: lastStop = sGraceful => stopLost = 0 is violated)
limitsWithoutTest.reason: model results (the first violates invariant 8, the second invariant 13); the code files the settled read's mail, covered by the first test of the graceful-stop row

limitsWithoutTest.text: claude-session-end-unrecorded-loss.tex: a settled stop that adds the dropped mail to lostN without reporting it in stopLost
limitsWithoutTest.reason: model result (invariant 15, lostN = lostBefore + stopLost, violated; conservation and lastStop = sGraceful => stopLost = 0 hold); the shipped model holds over 64,025 states

limitsWithoutTest.text: a crash after the relay gave session mail up and before the daemon stored it
limitsWithoutTest.reason: PL-1753; not representable in the model (the fetch and the storage are one step); a documented limit

limitsWithoutTest.text: claude-session-end-nopersist.tex: the records are not kept (the old forgetting behaviour) and the mail is stranded with no drop behind it
limitsWithoutTest.reason: model result (invariant 8, strandedN > 0 => dropCause in the drop causes, violated by MailArrive, ProcessLoss); the code keeps the records, covered by the restore rows above

limitsWithoutTest.text: RestoreRecord after TtyAgesOut: the restored session keeps the row's tty name and does not claim one; the reservation, if aged out, is not taken again
limitsWithoutTest.reason: code read: SessionRestore._open drops a record whose row is gone (dRowGone), and Session.register -> PresenceRow.ensure keeps an existing row's tty_name, claiming a name only when the row is missing. The model matches (RestoreRecord leaves ttyOwner as is). No test ages the name reservation under a stopped record or checks the restored name. A row that expires between the lookup and the registration would claim a new name; not modelled
